problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}=\frac{Ax+1}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{1}{x-1},
$$

where $A$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x.$
worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $A.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+x+3 & =(Ax+1)(x-1)+{x}^{2}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=2$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{2}+2+3 & =(A(2)+1)(2-1)+{2}^{2}+4 \\ 9 & =2A+1+8 \\ 9 & =2A+9 \\ A & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{0x+1}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{1}{x-1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|+C\end{aligned}
$$
